why: Next greater element on a circular array: walk the indices twice (i mod n) so elements near the end can find their answer at the start. Only the first pass pushes; the second pass only resolves waiting indices.
hints: How would you handle the wrap-around without building a new array?
Iterate j from 0 to 2n-1 and use i = j mod n; the second lap lets the stack see the beginning again after the end.
Stack of indices still waiting: while nums[top] < nums[i], pop and set its answer to nums[i]; push i only during the first lap. Unresolved indices keep -1. O(n).
pitfalls: Do not push during the second lap, or indices are processed twice.
The maximum value (and any copies of it) has no greater element: -1.
